title: Final norm + lm_head input MXFP8 quantize
description: The final RMSNorm output [4096,7168] is re-read to quantize it for the lm_head GEMM, with a separate scale swizzle.
bitwise_notes: RMSNorm reduction; exact amax.
dataflow: Same pattern as F2 for the head.
blockers: Separate op owners.

title: Inverse query RoPE (backward) fused with MXFP8 quantization of dq for wq_b backward
description: The query RoPE backward rotates dq [4096,128,192] in place, then wq_b's backward re-reads it to quantize rowwise and colwise (three scale swizzles). One kernel can rotate and quantize in a single pass; the bf16 dq has no other consumer.
bitwise_notes: Pointwise rotation + exact amax.
dataflow: flash-attn backward postprocess -> dq -> fused_mla_q_rope_ (in place) -> mxfp8_quantize -> wq_b dgrad/wgrad.
blockers: Recipe kernel + torchao quantizer; MXFP8LinearFunction must accept pre-quantized grad_output. Extending into the flash-attention dQ postprocess (fp32 accumulator -> MXFP8) would also remove the bf16 dq write (T3).

title: FSDP all-gather copy-out fused with MXFP8 weight quantization
description: After each layer's parameter all-gather, the gathered bf16 bucket is split into per-parameter bf16 weights (plus a cat for dim-1-sharded w13), and then every linear weight is re-read to produce MXFP8 data and 32x32 block scales (expert weights through a separate quantizer).
bitwise_notes: Block amax is a max-reduction (order-insensitive, exact), so a fused kernel can be bitwise identical; layout of the swizzled scales must match.
dataflow: split_with_sizes_copy writes every unsharded bf16 weight, which is consumed only by the weight quantizer (except norm weights and the bf16 router gate). Quantizing straight from the gathered buffer removes one bf16 write+read of every weight.
blockers: Copy-out belongs to the FSDP bucketing pass; weight quantization belongs to the MXFP8 linear (torchao) and dist_moe.prepare_mxfp8_weight; the gathered layout is shard-major (256 x shard) so the quantizer must read 32x32 tiles across shard boundaries.

title: Attention dQ postprocess + q RoPE backward + wq_b dY MXFP8 quantize
description: The attention backward accumulates dQ in fp32 [4096,128,192] and a postprocess kernel converts it to bf16; RoPE backward is then applied in place on the rope part, and the result is re-read to quantize it to MXFP8 for the wq_b backward GEMMs.
bitwise_notes: Pointwise cast and rotation plus exact amax; the dQ accumulation itself is untouched.
dataflow: Postprocess writes dq bf16 (201 MB), q_rope_ reads/writes it, quantize reads it again; one kernel reading the fp32 accumulator and writing fp8 rowwise+colwise removes three bf16 passes.
blockers: The postprocess kernel is internal to the flash-attention backward (torch_attn._varlen_attn_backward); needs a <callback> to replace its epilogue or to expose dQaccum.

title: HiMidLo router-gate backward: split, stack and weight-gradient accumulation in one pass
description: The gate's fp32 output gradient [4096,256] is split into three bf16 pieces with eight elementwise kernels and concatenated, the bf16 weight is stacked three times, and the weight gradient of three GEMMs is accumulated with two add_ kernels and a final cast. A single split kernel writing the stacked operand directly (and GEMM accumulation for dW) removes most of these launches.
bitwise_notes: Piece split is exact bit manipulation; the dW sum over three pieces must keep its order (or move into GEMM beta=1 accumulation, T3).
dataflow: router backward -> d gate (fp32) -> _to_copy/__lshift__/sub x2 -> cat -> mm (dgrad); cat(weight x3); mm x3 + add_ x2 -> _to_copy -> weight grad.
blockers: Small tensors: launch-bound (~2-4 us per kernel).

title: attention_norm + duplicate MXFP8 quantize for wq_a / wkv_a
description: Per layer, attention_norm normalizes the residual stream [4096,7168] and the normalized tensor is then quantized to MXFP8 twice (once for wq_a and once for wkv_a, identical results), each followed by a scale-swizzle kernel; dense layers also add the previous layer's MLP residual first, and layer 0 starts from the embedding gather.
bitwise_notes: RMSNorm row reduction order; exact amax.
dataflow: norm output -> two identical rowwise quantizations -> two swizzles; one kernel can normalize, quantize once, and write swizzled scales (plus the colwise copy, see B10).
blockers: Norm (aten _fused_rms_norm) and quantize (torchao) are separate custom ops inside different modules; the two linears do not know they share an input.

title: dist_moe dispatch-buffer copies and activation save/restore
description: Per MoE layer, the routed-expert forward copies the normalized tokens [4096,7168] into the dispatch buffer and again into an activation buffer for backward recompute; the backward copies them back into the dispatch buffer before recomputing the expert forward.
bitwise_notes: Copies only.
dataflow: The forward copies read the same input (ffn_norm output, which the program already keeps alive for the shared experts and router backward); the backward restore re-creates data that is still resident.
blockers: Library-internal: dist_moe keeps its own activation buffer for recompute decisions made on device; the dispatch buffer must be in symmetric memory.

title: q_norm + wq_b MXFP8 quantize
description: Per layer, q_norm normalizes the wq_a output [4096,1536] and the result is quantized to MXFP8 for the wq_b GEMM with a separate scale swizzle.
bitwise_notes: RMSNorm reduction; exact amax.
dataflow: norm output feeds the quantizer and is saved for backward (re-quantized in B10).
blockers: Separate op owners.

title: Colwise re-quantization of saved bf16 linear inputs in backward
description: For the linears whose inputs are saved in bf16 (wq_a, wkv_a, wq_b, wo, w13, lm_head), the backward re-reads the saved activation to quantize it along tokens for the weight-gradient GEMM; the attention_norm output is quantized twice (for wq_a and wkv_a).
bitwise_notes: Exact amax; the forward quantizer can emit the colwise copy from the same 32x32 tile.
dataflow: The forward quantize kernels (F2/F3/F4/F6) already read these tensors; emitting the colwise fp8 copy there costs only its write and removes the backward read (and the duplicate wq_a/wkv_a pass).
blockers: Changes what is saved for backward (fp8 colwise instead of bf16) -- the bf16 copy may still be needed by other consumers (router gate, aux loss); torchao's saved-format choice (306 bf16 vs 122 mxfp8 linears).

title: SwiGLU + w2 MXFP8 quantize
description: Per layer, silu_and_mul turns the w13 output [4096,2,2048] (dense: [4096,2,18432]) into [4096,2048] bf16, which is re-read to quantize it to MXFP8 (both orientations) for the w2 GEMM.
bitwise_notes: Pointwise; exact amax.
dataflow: silu_and_mul output only feeds the quantizer (and is not otherwise saved, since the fp8 colwise copy is saved for backward).
blockers: Custom op + torchao quantizer.

title: Flash-attention forward epilogue writes the MXFP8 copy of the attention output for wo
description: wo's forward re-reads the attention output [4096,16384] bf16 to quantize it to MXFP8 rowwise and swizzle its scales. The attention forward already holds each output tile and can write the MXFP8 layout next to the bf16 output (which backward still needs).
bitwise_notes: Requires changing the FA4 CuTe kernel epilogue; amax exact.
dataflow: flash-attn forward -> O (bf16, saved) -> mxfp8_quantize -> wo scaled_mm.
blockers: FA4 kernel is external (flash_attn.cute); per-head output tiles must cover whole 32-element blocks (they do: head dim 128).

title: attention_norm backward with fused wq_a/wkv_a gradient sum, residual add and the previous layer's w2 dy quantization (cross-layer)
description: wq_a's and wkv_a's input gradients are summed by an add, attention_norm's RMSNorm backward runs as two kernels, a separate add_ accumulates the residual gradient, and the previous block's shared-expert (or dense) w2 backward then re-reads the result to quantize it to MXFP8. One row-wise kernel can produce the bf16 residual gradient and its MXFP8 layouts.
shapes_dtypes: bf16 [4096,7168] partial grads x2, norm input, residual grad -> bf16 [4096,7168] + fp8e4m3 rowwise/colwise + e8m0
bitwise_notes: Accumulation order of the two dgrads and RMSNorm-backward reductions must be matched.
dataflow: wq_a dgrad + wkv_a dgrad (add) -> rmsnorm_backward -> + residual (add_) -> [previous block] shared_experts.w2 mxfp8_quantize(dy) -> w2 dgrad/wgrad; the bf16 result also feeds the previous block's routed-expert broadcast_and_scale and its ffn_norm residual add.
blockers: Crosses the block/FSDP-unit boundary (post-backward reduce-scatter and pre-backward all-gather <callback> fire in between); partial gradients come from two MXFP8Linear autograd op(s).

title: q_norm forward fused with wq_b MXFP8 quantization
description: q_norm normalises the wq_a output [4096,1536] and wq_b re-reads the result to quantize it. One kernel can write the bf16 normed tensor (saved for wq_b's wgrad) and its MXFP8 layout.
bitwise_notes: RMSNorm row reduction order.
dataflow: wq_a scaled_mm -> rmsnorm -> mxfp8_quantize -> wq_b scaled_mm.
blockers: Launch-bound small tensors.

title: Attention residual add + ffn_norm + w13 MXFP8 quantization
description: After wo, the block adds the attention output to the residual, ffn_norm normalises it and shared_experts.w13 (or the dense w13) re-reads the normed tensor to quantize it. One row-wise kernel can write the residual, the bf16 normed tensor (saved, and read by the router gate and the dispatch copy) and its MXFP8 layout.
shapes_dtypes: bf16 [4096,7168] x2 -> bf16 residual, bf16 normed, fp8e4m3 [4096,7168] + e8m0
bitwise_notes: RMSNorm row reduction order; add and amax exact.
dataflow: wo scaled_mm -> + residual (add) -> rmsnorm -> mxfp8_quantize (w13), normed also -> router gate mm, Dist-MoE dispatch copy.
blockers: Three modules (block, ffn_norm, MXFP8Linear); the add could alternatively be wo's GEMM epilogue (T3).

title: Attention-backward preprocess (rowsum(dO*O), dQaccum zero) in wo dgrad GEMM epilogue
description: The flash-attention backward preprocess re-reads the attention output O and its gradient dO [4096,128,128] to compute the per-row dot product and zero the fp32 dQ accumulator; dO is produced by the wo dgrad GEMM immediately before.
bitwise_notes: Needs the GEMM; the row dot product over head_dim=128 must use the preprocess's fp32 summation order.
dataflow: Each GEMM output tile holds dO for complete head rows (128 columns = one head), so the epilogue can load the matching O tile and emit rowsum(dO*O) per (token, head) while storing dO.
blockers: cuBLAS (nvjet) GEMM has no custom epilogue; flash-attention owns the preprocess and its layout of dpsum/LSE; zeroing dQaccum is still needed unless the main kernel initializes it.

title: FSDP reduce-scatter copy-in: shard-interleave cat of w13 grads + bucket pack
description: Before each layer's gradient reduce-scatter, every weight gradient is chunked along its shard axis and copied into one flat bf16 bucket; the dim-1-sharded w13 gradients ([2, 2048|18432, 7168]) are first re-laid out by a 256-input cat into [512, 8|72, 7168] and then packed again.
bitwise_notes: Pure copies into fixed offsets; any order of writes gives identical bytes.
dataflow: Each wgrad GEMM output and norm-weight grad is read once by chunk_cat and written once into the reduce-scatter input bucket; the w13 grad is read and rewritten twice (cat, then chunk_cat). A single multi-tensor pack kernel that applies the dim-1 shard interleave while packing reads each grad once and writes the bucket once.
blockers: Bucketing pass (bucketing._pre_bucket_reduce_scatter) and DTensor redistribute own the layout; the dim-1 interleave comes from Shard(1) placement of w13. Further step (T3): let wgrad GEMMs write straight into bucket offsets.
source: torchtitan/experiments/graph_trainer/simple_fsdp.py:366 (Shard redistribute backward, w13 interleave cat); bucketing._pre_bucket_reduce_scatter from <transform>

title: Router gate backward GEMM operand packing and fp32 weight-grad accumulation
description: The 3-term (hi/mid/lo) bf16 router-gate backward replicates the [256,7168] gate weight three times for the input-gradient GEMM and runs three weight-gradient GEMMs whose fp32 outputs are accumulated by two adds and cast to bf16.
bitwise_notes: Accumulating the three products in the GEMM epilogue (beta=1) keeps the same fp32 add order; a single K-concatenated GEMM would not be bitwise identical.
dataflow: <value> output only feeds one GEMM; mm outputs only feed the add_ chain; the final cast only feeds the gradient output.
blockers: mm has no accumulate-into epilogue; replicated-weight cat is an artifact of expressing the 3-way split as one GEMM.

title: ffn_norm backward with fused MoE input-gradient combine/accumulation, residual add and MXFP8 dy for wo
description: The gradient of ffn_norm's output arrives as three partial gradients: the routed experts' per-slot dgrad [4096,8,7168] summed over K, the shared-expert w13 dgrad and the router gate dgrad, accumulated by two separate adds. Then RMSNorm backward, a separate residual add_, and wo's backward re-reads the result to quantize it. One row-wise kernel can sum the partials, run the norm backward, add the residual gradient and write both bf16 and MXFP8 (rowwise+colwise) outputs.
shapes_dtypes: dX per slot bf16 [4096,8,7168]; partial grads bf16 [4096,7168] x2; ffn_norm input bf16 [4096,7168]; residual grad bf16 [4096,7168]; out bf16 [4096,7168] + MXFP8 rowwise/colwise
bitwise_notes: K-sum order of scale_and_sum, the autograd accumulation order ((shared + routed) + gate), the RMSNorm-backward row reduction and the weight-gradient column partials must be matched.
dataflow: dgrad combine buffer -> scale_and_sum -> + shared w13 dgrad (add) -> + gate dgrad (add_) -> rmsnorm_backward -> + residual grad (add_) -> mxfp8_quantize -> wo dgrad/wgrad GEMMs; the bf16 result also flows to attention_norm backward's residual add.
blockers: Partial gradients come from different autograd op(s) (Dist-MoE custom op, MXFP8 linear, HiMidLo linear), so fusing needs a custom backward for the whole MoE block; scale_and_sum is a Dist-MoE kernel.

title: FSDP all-gather copy-out fused with MXFP8 weight quantization of each block's unsharded weights
description: After each transformer block's parameter all-gather (forward unshard and backward re-unshard), the rank-major gathered bf16 buffer is de-interleaved into per-parameter bf16 tensors, w13 is reassembled and made contiguous, then every MXFP8 linear weight is quantized to 32x32-block MXFP8 into a temporary and copied into the persistent operand storage (expert w13/w2 likewise via Dist-MoE weight preparation). One kernel per block could read the gathered buffer once and write the persistent MXFP8 operands (and bf16 only for the unquantized norm/router/bias parameters).
shapes_dtypes: MoE block: gathered bf16 [256, 915520] (dense params, 234M elems) + [4, 44040192] (4 local experts' w13 [4,2,2048,7168] and w2 [4,7168,2048]); outputs fp8e4m3 qdata + e8m0 swizzled scales (2 layouts) per linear weight; dense blocks [256, 2284608]; (norm, lm_head) group [256, 3619868] with lm_head [129280, 7168]
bitwise_notes: Pure data movement plus per-32x32-block amax (max is order-independent, exact). Bitwise identity only needs the same block-scale rounding as the torchao/Dist-MoE quantizers and correct rank-major addressing.
dataflow: all_gather output -> split_with_sizes_copy -> (cat reassembly, clone for dim-1 shards) -> triton 32x32 quantize/swizzle (temp) -> copy_ into persistent operands; FSDP releases the bf16 per-parameter tensors right after quantization, so the bf16 round trip and the temp->persistent copy have no other consumer.
blockers: Spans FSDP internals (copy-out runs before fsdp_post_all_gather), torchtitan's MXFP8 FSDP tensor subclass and Dist-MoE's weight preparation; needs a format-aware all-gather output <callback>. Same work is repeated for the backward re-unshard (reshard_after_forward); keeping the MXFP8 operands from forward to backward would remove the backward half entirely at a memory cost.

title: Routed-expert backward: fold score gradient and dy broadcast into the expert GEMMs (no [T,K,D] materialisation)
description: broadcast_and_scale reads dy [4096,7168], the recomputed per-slot expert outputs x [4096,8,7168] and the scores, writing dx = dy*score for every (token, k) slot [4096,8,7168] and dscore = <dy, x>. The score gradient can be computed in the epilogue of the recompute fprop GEMM that produces x, and the scaled broadcast can be generated in the dgrad GEMM's operand load, so neither 470 MB tensor needs to be written and re-read.
bitwise_notes: Needs grouped GEMM epilogue/prologue changes; dscore is a 7168-long dot product whose summation order must match the Triton kernel.
dataflow: recompute fprop GEMM -> x[T,K,D] (written to the combine buffer) -> broadcast_and_scale(dy, scores, x) -> dx[T,K,D] (dispatch buffer) -> dgrad GEMM reads dx from peers.
blockers: Dist-MoE owns the kernels; in real EP the expert GEMM runs on the expert-owning rank, so its epilogue needs the source token's dy (remote read over symmetric memory). Fake-PG GEMM times here process only rank 0's local rows, so the GEMM side is not representative.

title: k RoPE / k-v split as wkv_b GEMM epilogue
description: The wkv_b GEMM writes [4096,128,256] bf16 (k_nope|v per head), and a separate kernel reads it back with k_pe [4096,64] to build k [4096,128,192] (with RoPE on the shared k_pe broadcast to all heads) and v.
bitwise_notes: Needs the GEMM; RoPE and copies are pointwise.
dataflow: Each output tile row is one token's (k_nope, v) for a head; the epilogue can write k_nope into k, append rotated k_pe and write v directly.
blockers: cuBLAS nvjet GEMM without custom epilogue; output split into two tensors with different strides.

title: Reduce-scatter output cast to fp32 + param.grad clone
description: After each layer's reduce-scatter, every gradient shard is cast from bf16 to fp32 by its own kernel (848 casts), and after the step's backward the runtime clones each fp32 gradient again to initialize param.grad (848 copies).
bitwise_notes: Casts and copies only.
dataflow: Each reduce-scatter output shard is read once and written as fp32; the clone then reads and writes it again. A single multi-tensor kernel per bucket can cast directly into the param.grad storage.
blockers: The casts are program outputs (one per parameter); the clone is done outside the program by the gradient-accumulation helper (clone_grads_to_initialize_param_grad).
source: torchtitan/experiments/graph_trainer/simple_fsdp.py:366 (gradient cast to fp32 param dtype); graph_pp/runner.py:531 + common_utils.py:303-326 (param.grad clone)

title: MLA KV backward pack fused with MXFP8 quantization of the packed KV gradient for wkv_b backward
description: The fused KV-backward kernel packs dK-nope and dV into the bf16 kv gradient [4096,128,256] and reduces/inverse-rotates dK-rope; wkv_b's backward then re-reads that 268 MB tensor to quantize it rowwise and colwise to MXFP8 (plus two scale swizzles). The pack kernel can emit both MXFP8 layouts directly; the bf16 kv gradient has no other consumer.
bitwise_notes: dK-rope reduction over 128 heads must keep the existing kernel's order; MXFP8 amax per 32 elements is exact.
dataflow: flash-attn backward -> dK, dV -> _fused_kv_backward -> grad_kv (bf16) -> mxfp8_quantize (rowwise+colwise) -> wkv_b dgrad and wgrad GEMMs.
blockers: The KV pack is a recipe Triton kernel and the quantizer is torchao's; MXFP8LinearFunction would need to accept a pre-quantized grad_output.

title: MLA kv backward + wkv_b dY MXFP8 quantize
description: The attention backward's dK [4096,128,192] and dV [4096,128,128] are re-packed into the wkv_b output gradient [4096,128,256] plus the summed k_pe gradient [4096,64], and that gradient is then re-read to quantize it to MXFP8 (both orientations) with a separate scale-swizzle kernel.
bitwise_notes: k_pe grad is a sum over 128 heads (order must match fused_mla_kv_backward); quantization amax is exact.
dataflow: fused_mla_kv_backward writes the bf16 [4096,32768] tensor that only the quantizer reads; quantizing in the same kernel removes a 268 MB write+read per layer.
blockers: Two custom kernels from different owners (fused MLA override, torchao mxfp8_quantize); the quantizer needs 32-row blocks for the colwise orientation, so the fused kernel must tile 32 tokens x 32 features.

title: Fused cross-entropy forward + backward with lm_head dY quantize
description: The lm_head logits [4096,129280] bf16 are upcast to fp32, log-softmaxed and gathered for the loss, then in backward the fp32 softmax gradient is rebuilt, cast back to bf16 and quantized to MXFP8 for the lm_head backward GEMMs.
shapes_dtypes: logits bf16 [4096,129280] -> fp32 (2.1 GB) -> log_softmax fp32; grad fp32 -> bf16 -> fp8 [4096,129280] + scales
bitwise_notes: Max and sum-exp reductions over the vocabulary must follow the same order; one fused kernel can do fwd and bwd because the loss gradient is a known constant scale.
dataflow: Forward needs per-row max/LSE and the target logit; backward needs softmax - onehot. Reading the bf16 logits once can produce the loss, and the fp8 gradient in the same pass.
blockers: Loss function boundary and the autograd split between forward and backward; the grad scale (1/num_tokens) must be known at forward time.

title: FSDP all-gather copy-in with fp32->bf16 cast and pad
description: Before each layer's parameter all-gather, the fp32 parameter shards are cast to bf16 and packed into the all-gather input buffer by a multi-tensor kernel, while unevenly sharded parameters (e.g. wkv_a's [3,7168] shard) take a separate cast + pad pair.
bitwise_notes: Casts and copies only.
dataflow: The odd-shaped shard is cast and padded into a temporary and then copied again into the bucket; folding it into the multi-tensor copy-in removes two kernels per layer; small buckets are launch-bound.
blockers: Padding is decided by DTensor/simple_fsdp for uneven shards; the bucketing pass owns the copy-in.

title: tok_embeddings: embedding lookup directly from the gathered buffer (skip the full-table copy-out)
description: FSDP copies the gathered 1.85 GB embedding table out of the rank-major all-gather buffer before the lookup reads only 4096 rows. The lookup can index the gathered buffer directly.
bitwise_notes: Pure gather.
dataflow: all_gather -> split_with_sizes_copy (full table) -> embedding (4096 rows).
blockers: FSDP materialises unsharded parameters before forward; the embedding module would need the rank-major layout.

title: Horizontal GEMM fusion of wq_a and wkv_a (shared input) in forward and input-gradient
description: wq_a [7168->1536] and wkv_a [7168->576] read the same normed input; their forward GEMMs can be one GEMM with N=2112, and their input-gradient GEMMs (whose outputs are summed) one GEMM with K=2112 over the concatenated output gradients, which also removes the summing add.
bitwise_notes: The merged dgrad accumulates both products inside one GEMM K-loop, which changes rounding versus two GEMMs plus a bf16 add (not bitwise without a split-K order match); the forward concatenation is bitwise-safe.
dataflow: attention_norm -> quantize (shared) -> wq_a GEMM, wkv_a GEMM; backward: q_norm-bwd output -> wq_a dgrad, kv_norm-bwd/cat output -> wkv_a dgrad -> add.
blockers: Two separate MXFP8Linear modules and FSDP parameters (weights would need a stacked parameter or a grouped GEMM); the dgrad merge changes numerics unless done as a grouped GEMM with a fused bf16 add.

title: Router aux-loss forward statistics
description: Per MoE layer, the load-balance auxiliary loss converts the selection mask to fp32, sums it over tokens, L2-normalizes the scores, sums them over tokens and combines them into a scalar loss term; about 23 kernels, most on [4096,256] or scalars.
shapes_dtypes: mask bool [4096,256] -> fp32; scores fp32 [4096,256]; column sums [256]; scalars
bitwise_notes: Column sums over 4096 tokens and norms must keep the reduction order (2-kernel split reductions today).
dataflow: Reads the same sigmoid scores and selection mask that the router (F10) already holds; can be computed as a by-product of the routing kernel with a second-stage column reduction.
blockers: Separate function boundary from the router; cross-token column reductions need a two-pass or ordered reduction for determinism.

title: Dist-MoE forward dispatch staging: padding mask, routing/activation copies and planning in fewer kernels
description: Before the routed-expert GEMMs, two masked_fills apply the padding mask to the top-k ids and scores, the normed tokens and routing are copied into the symmetric dispatch buffer, five small planning kernels (metadata gather, routing split/prefix/combine, forward plan) run, the dispatch buffer is copied into the activation buffer and a cat packs scalars. These read the same routing tensors and the same 58.7 MB token block.
shapes_dtypes: normed x bf16 [4096,7168]; topk ids int64 / scores fp32 [4096,8]; dispatch buffer bf16 [4096,8,7168] capacity
bitwise_notes: Slot assignment uses prefix sums over routed tokens (integer, order-defined).
dataflow: router outputs -> masked_fill x2 -> copy_routing_and_dispatch (x -> dispatch buffer) -> routing split/prefix/combine -> plan -> copy_dispatch_to_activation -> grouped GEMMs.
blockers: Dist-MoE internals and the EP synchronisation protocol (barriers between planning steps); under the fake PG some kernels only see rank 0's rows.

title: ffn_norm backward block: grad sum + top-k reduce + RMSNorm backward + residual add + wo dY quantize
description: Per layer, the gradient of the ffn_norm output is the sum of the router-gate, routed-expert (top-k reduced over 8 routes) and shared-expert input gradients; it feeds RMSNorm backward, whose input gradient is added to the residual gradient and then quantized to MXFP8 for the wo backward GEMMs.
bitwise_notes: Sum over K routes and the RMSNorm row/column reductions must keep their order; the separate bf16 roundings of each add must be reproduced.
dataflow: reduce_from_topk -> add -> add -> rms_norm_backward (+ weight-grad column reduction kernel) -> add residual grad -> mxfp8_quantize -> scale swizzle; every intermediate [4096,7168] tensor has exactly one consumer inside the chain.
blockers: reduce_from_topk lives inside dist_moe.block_scaled_backward; the RMSNorm weight-grad needs a cross-token reduction (second kernel today).

title: SwiGLU backward + w13 dY MXFP8 quantize
description: Per layer, the SwiGLU backward produces the w13 output gradient [4096,2,2048] (dense: [4096,2,18432]) in bf16, which is re-read to quantize it to MXFP8 for the w13 backward GEMMs.
bitwise_notes: Pointwise SwiGLU grad; exact amax.
dataflow: silu_and_mul_backward output has a single consumer (the quantizer).
blockers: Custom op (torchtitan.silu_and_mul_backward) and torchao quantizer are separate kernels.

title: q_norm backward fused with wq_a dy quantization
description: q_norm's RMSNorm backward (two kernels) writes d(q_a) [4096,1536] and wq_a's backward re-reads it to quantize it. One kernel can emit MXFP8 directly; the bf16 gradient has no other consumer.
bitwise_notes: RMSNorm-backward reduction order.
dataflow: wq_b dgrad -> rmsnorm_backward (+reduce_rows) -> mxfp8_quantize -> wq_a GEMMs.
blockers: Launch-bound; two autograd op(s).

title: kv_norm (strided slice) + wkv_b MXFP8 quantize
description: Per layer, kv_norm normalizes the first 512 columns of the wkv_a output [4096,576] (a strided slice that costs an extra copy kernel), and the result is quantized to MXFP8 in both orientations with two scale-swizzle kernels.
bitwise_notes: RMSNorm reduction order; exact amax.
dataflow: Slice copy -> norm -> quantize -> 2 swizzles; all on a 4 MB tensor.
blockers: aten fused RMSNorm requires a contiguous input; separate torchao quantizer.

title: Dist-MoE grouped-GEMM prepare kernels folded into their GEMMs
description: Each routed-expert grouped GEMM (forward fprop dispatch and SwiGLU-combine GEMMs, their backward recompute, dgrad and wgrad GEMMs) is preceded by a separate ~5 us 'prepare' kernel launched by Dist-MoE. Folding the preparation into the persistent GEMM's prologue removes 2 launches per MoE layer in forward and 6 in backward.
shapes_dtypes: routing/plan metadata (int32) for 4 local experts; MXFP8 operands of [rows, 7168] x [4, 4096 | 2048, 7168]
bitwise_notes: Inside the grouped GEMM implementation; no floating-point arithmetic is reordered if the prepare work moves into the GEMM prologue.
dataflow: Dist-MoE plan -> prepare kernel -> grouped GEMM (consumes the prepared state only).
blockers: Dist-MoE CuTe kernels; the prepare step may exist to publish state to peers before the dispatch GEMM starts (cross-rank ordering).

title: MLA query RoPE applied in the wq_b GEMM epilogue instead of a full-tensor copy
description: fused_mla_q rotates the 64 rope dims of each of 128 heads but, being out of place, copies the whole query [4096,128,192] bf16 (201 MB read + 201 MB write). The wq_b GEMM epilogue can rotate the rope columns in registers before storing q.
bitwise_notes: Needs the MXFP8 GEMM epilogue; the rotation itself is pointwise (fp32 math then bf16 round must match the Triton kernel).
dataflow: wq_b scaled_mm -> q (bf16) -> fused_mla_q_rope (copy + rotate) -> flash attention.
blockers: cuBLAS nvjet MXFP8 GEMM has no custom epilogue; requires a CUTLASS/CuTe GEMM. An in-place rotation of only the rope columns (134 MB, ~19 us) is the non-GEMM fallback but the recipe avoids it because autograd's CopySlices would materialise the projection.

title: Residual-stream update + RMSNorm + shared MXFP8 quantization of the next projections (cross-layer)
description: At the end of each MoE block, scale_and_sum combines the 8 routed expert outputs [4096,8,7168] with the router scores, a separate add adds the shared-expert output and another adds the residual; the next block's attention_norm then normalises the result, and wq_a and wkv_a each quantize the same normed tensor to MXFP8 (two identical quantizations). One row-wise kernel can do the combine, both adds, the RMSNorm and a single quantization (also the final norm feeding lm_head).
shapes_dtypes: x per slot bf16 [4096,8,7168], scores fp32 [4096,8], shared out / residual bf16 [4096,7168] -> residual bf16 [4096,7168], normed bf16 [4096,7168] (saved for wq_a/wkv_a wgrad), fp8e4m3 [4096,7168] + e8m0 [4096,224]
bitwise_notes: K-sum order of scale_and_sum, the add order (routed + shared, then residual) and the RMSNorm row reduction must be matched; quantize amax is exact.
dataflow: combine buffer -> scale_and_sum -> + shared (add) -> + residual (add) -> [next block] rmsnorm -> mxfp8_quantize (wq_a) and mxfp8_quantize (wkv_a) of the same tensor -> GEMMs.
blockers: Crosses the block boundary and the FSDP unit boundary (next block's pre-forward all-gather <callback> fire in between); scale_and_sum lives in Dist-MoE; the two quantizations are inside two separate MXFP8Linear modules (needs a shared-input quantization cache).

title: wq_a / wkv_a sibling GEMMs on the same normed input
description: wq_a [7168->1536] and wkv_a [7168->576] both consume the same quantized attention_norm output, and in backward both produce input gradients that are summed; the N=576 GEMM runs at half its roofline.
bitwise_notes: Concatenating N in forward is bitwise identical per output column; concatenating K in dgrad changes the fp32 accumulation (sum of two GEMMs + bf16 add today).
dataflow: Forward: one GEMM with N=2112 reads the activation once. Backward: [dq_a | dkv_a] x [Wq_a ; Wkv_a] gives dX directly and removes the add in B1.
blockers: Two separate MXFP8Linear modules with separate FSDP parameters; weight concatenation needs a fused parameter or a grouped GEMM.

title: Embedding dense backward
description: The token-embedding backward accumulates the [4096,7168] input gradient into a [129280,7168] bf16 table gradient with the deterministic sort-based path (21 kernels).
bitwise_notes: Accumulation order for repeated token ids must match the deterministic implementation.
dataflow: Zero-fill of the table and the segment-sum can be one pass that also writes straight into the reduce-scatter bucket.
blockers: Deterministic mode forces sort + segment reduction.

title: FSDP reduce-scatter copy-in: dim-1 shard reorder cat folded into chunk_cat
description: In each block's post-backward, the shared-expert (or dense FFN) w13 gradient [2, F, 7168], sharded on dim 1, is chunked into 256 pieces and concatenated (four batched-cat launches over 512 strided inputs) before chunk_cat copies all gradients into the rank-major reduce-scatter buffer. A chunk_cat that addresses each gradient along its own shard dimension writes the buffer in one pass.
bitwise_notes: Order-defined data movement, no arithmetic.
dataflow: unsharded grads (autograd outputs) -> torch.cat(chunks along dim 1) -> _chunk_cat into flat RS input -> reduce_scatter; the cat output is consumed only by chunk_cat.
blockers: FSDP owns the copy-in; needs per-tensor shard-dim support in fsdp::chunk_cat (upstream change). The chunk_cat kernel itself runs at 0.65-0.9x of its own roofline for the 1.85 GB lm_head gradient.

title: MoE router forward: sigmoid, biased group-limited top-k, gather/normalize, routing map, token counts and load-balance statistics
description: From the fp32 gate logits [4096, 256], the router runs ~47 small kernels per MoE layer: sigmoid, expert-bias add, per-group top-2 and group sum, group top-4, mask, top-8, gather of unbiased scores, normalisation and scaling, one-hot routing map, token-per-expert counts, and the microbatch load-balance loss statistics (counts, L1-normalised score sums, f*p). One row-wise kernel (plus a small cross-token reduction) produces all of them.
shapes_dtypes: gate logits fp32 [4096,256]; [4096,8,32] group view; topk scores fp32 [4096,8], ids int64 [4096,8]; routing map bool [4096,256]; counts fp32 [256]
bitwise_notes: Top-k selection with sorted=False must reproduce torch.topk's tie-breaking and output order (order-sensitive); the aux-loss column sums over 4096 tokens need the reduce_kernel's order (T1).
dataflow: gate mm (fp32 out) -> sigmoid -> +bias -> topk(2) per group -> sum -> topk(4 groups) -> scatter mask -> masked_fill -> topk(8) -> gather(scores) -> sum/div/mul; scores also -> aux-loss normalize/sum; routing_map -> sum -> tokens_per_expert add_. All intermediates are [4096,<=256] and consumed only inside the router.
blockers: torch.topk on [4096,256] costs ~72 us per call (radix-select gatherTopK) and three top-k calls dominate; deterministic mode; the aux-loss reduction crosses tokens (needs a second pass or atomics with fixed order).

title: RoPE position bound check hoisted out of the per-layer attention (cross-layer)
description: Every attention layer re-checks that all 4096 positions are below the rope cache size with three kernels (le, all, _assert_async) on the same positions tensor. One check per step suffices.
bitwise_notes: Boolean all-reduction (exact).
dataflow: positions -> le -> all -> _assert_async, repeated 61 times on the same input.
blockers: Lives in each attention module's forward; hoisting needs the check at the model or data level.

title: Attention residual add + ffn_norm + w13 MXFP8 quantize
description: Per layer, the wo output is added to the residual stream, normalized by ffn_norm, and the normalized tensor is quantized to MXFP8 for the shared-expert (or dense) w13 GEMM with a separate scale swizzle.
bitwise_notes: RMSNorm reduction order; the add's bf16 rounding must precede the norm.
dataflow: add -> rms_norm -> quantize -> swizzle; h and the normed tensor are still needed (residual, router, routed experts, backward).
blockers: Three different op owners (aten add, aten fused rms norm, torchao quantize); the add could alternatively become the wo GEMM epilogue (T3).

title: q RoPE as wq_b GEMM epilogue
description: The wq_b GEMM writes q [4096,128,192] in bf16 and a separate kernel reads it back to apply RoPE to the last 64 dims of every head and rewrite the whole tensor.
bitwise_notes: Needs the GEMM; the rotation is pointwise in fp32 and can match bitwise.
dataflow: RoPE pairs (2 adjacent features) lie inside one output tile row, so the epilogue can rotate before the store.
blockers: cuBLAS nvjet kernels have no custom epilogue; needs a CUTLASS/CuTe MXFP8 GEMM with an epilogue visitor.

title: Embedding backward scattered directly into the reduce-scatter buffer
description: The deterministic embedding backward zero-fills a [129280, 7168] bf16 gradient (1.85 GB) and accumulates the 4096 token rows with a sort-based scatter, then FSDP's chunk_cat copies the whole table into the reduce-scatter buffer. Zero-filling the reduce-scatter buffer and scattering the rows into its rank-major layout removes the full-table copy.
shapes_dtypes: grad out bf16 [4096,7168]; token ids int64 [4096]; table grad bf16 [129280,7168]; RS input bf16 [256, 3619840]
bitwise_notes: Duplicate token ids accumulate; the deterministic sorted accumulation order must be preserved.
dataflow: d embedding output -> embedding_backward (memset + sort + scatter-add) -> table grad -> chunk_cat -> reduce_scatter.
blockers: FSDP owns the copy-in; the autograd embedding backward allocates its own gradient.

title: kv_norm forward (without the contiguous clone) fused with wkv_b MXFP8 quantization
description: kv_latent is a strided slice of the wkv_a output [4096,576]; it is cloned to be contiguous, normalised, and wkv_b quantizes it rowwise and colwise (its input is saved in MXFP8). One kernel can read the slice in place and write only the MXFP8 layouts.
bitwise_notes: RMSNorm row reduction order.
dataflow: wkv_a scaled_mm -> split -> clone -> rmsnorm -> mxfp8_quantize (+2 swizzles) -> wkv_b scaled_mm.
blockers: Launch-bound small tensors; the norm backward needs its input saved (can be the strided view).

title: SwiGLU backward fused with MXFP8 quantization of d(h13) for w13 backward
description: silu_and_mul_backward writes d(h13) [4096, 2F] bf16 and w13's backward re-reads it to quantize rowwise and colwise (three swizzles). The SwiGLU backward kernel can emit the MXFP8 layouts directly; the bf16 gradient has no other consumer.
bitwise_notes: Pointwise math + exact amax.
dataflow: w2 dgrad GEMM -> dh -> silu_and_mul_backward(h13) -> d h13 -> mxfp8_quantize -> w13 dgrad/wgrad.
blockers: Recipe Triton kernel + torchao quantizer; MXFP8LinearFunction must accept pre-quantized grad_output.

title: q_norm backward + wq_a dY quantize
description: Per layer, q_norm's RMSNorm backward (two kernels on [4096,1536]) produces the wq_a output gradient, which is re-read to quantize it to MXFP8 for the wq_a backward GEMMs.
bitwise_notes: RMSNorm reductions; exact amax.
dataflow: rms bwd output has a single consumer (quantize).
blockers: Separate op owners; weight-grad column reduction needs a second pass.

title: MoE top-k combine + shared-expert add + residual add
description: Per MoE layer, the routed-expert outputs [4096,8,7168] are weighted and summed over the 8 routes, then added to the shared-expert output and to the residual stream as three separate passes over [4096,7168].
shapes_dtypes: route-wise bf16 [4096,8,7168] (470 MB), weights fp32 [4096,8], shared out bf16 [4096,7168], residual bf16 [4096,7168] -> layer output bf16 [4096,7168]
bitwise_notes: fp32 accumulation over K=8 in the library's order, then two bf16-rounded adds that must be reproduced separately.
dataflow: scale_and_sum writes y [4096,7168] that only <value> reads; <value>'s output is read only by <value>; the layer output then feeds the next attention_norm (F2) and the residual.
blockers: The combine runs inside dist_moe.block_scaled_forward after an EP barrier; adding the shared output requires passing it into the library or exposing the combine buffer.

title: MoE router forward: sigmoid + bias + group-limited top-k + normalize + expert counts
description: Per MoE layer, the router turns gate logits [4096,256] fp32 into 8 expert ids and weights per token via sigmoid, bias add, group top-2 sums, top-4 groups, masked top-8, gather, normalization and route scaling, then counts tokens per expert; about 28 small kernels including three top-k calls.
bitwise_notes: Top-k tie-breaking and index order must match torch.topk; the per-expert count is an integer reduction (exact).
dataflow: All ops consume the same [4096,256] score row of a token; a one-CTA-per-token-block kernel can do sigmoid, bias, group selection, final top-8, gather, normalization and the masked_fill of padded rows in registers and write only ids, weights, the selection mask and counts.
blockers: Must reproduce torch.topk ordering bitwise; the per-expert count update (add_ into a buffer) needs an atomic-free reduction for determinism.

title: SwiGLU forward fused with MXFP8 quantization of the w2 input
description: silu_and_mul writes h [4096,F] bf16 whose only consumer is w2's forward quantization (w2 saves its input in MXFP8, rowwise for fprop and colwise for wgrad). The SwiGLU kernel can write both MXFP8 layouts directly.
bitwise_notes: Pointwise + exact amax.
dataflow: w13 scaled_mm -> h13 -> silu_and_mul -> h -> mxfp8_quantize (rowwise+colwise, colwise saved) -> w2 scaled_mm.
blockers: Recipe Triton kernel + torchao quantizer; MXFP8LinearFunction must accept pre-quantized input.

title: Fused cross-entropy forward/backward on bf16 logits, emitting MXFP8 dlogits for lm_head backward
description: The loss upcasts the bf16 logits [4096,129280] to fp32, runs log_softmax (writes a 2.1 GB fp32 tensor saved for backward) and nll_loss; backward zero-fills a 2.1 GB gradient, scatters -1/N, runs the log-softmax backward, downcasts to bf16 and lm_head's backward re-reads it to quantize. A fused cross-entropy keeps only the per-row logsumexp from the forward and writes the MXFP8 (rowwise+colwise) logit gradient directly in the backward.
shapes_dtypes: logits bf16 [4096,129280]; fp32 copies [4096,129280]; labels int64 [4096]; dlogits bf16 [4096,129280] -> fp8e4m3 rowwise/colwise
bitwise_notes: Row max/sum-exp reductions over 129280 must reproduce the softmax kernel's order for bitwise identity.
dataflow: lm_head GEMM -> logits -> _to_copy fp32 -> _log_softmax -> nll_loss -> loss; backward: zero_ + nll_loss_backward -> _log_softmax_backward_data -> _to_copy bf16 -> mxfp8_quantize -> lm_head dgrad/wgrad.
blockers: Crosses the loss/model boundary and lm_head's MXFP8 autograd Function (needs pre-quantized grad_output); could also be the lm_head GEMM epilogue (T3).

title: kv_norm backward + split backward cat + wkv_a dy quantization
description: kv_norm's backward clones its non-contiguous input slice, runs two kernels, the split backward concatenates d(kv_latent) [4096,512] with d(k_pe) [4096,64], and wkv_a's backward quantizes the [4096,576] result. One kernel can read the slice in place, write into the [4096,576] gradient and emit MXFP8.
bitwise_notes: RMSNorm-backward reductions (row and weight column) order.
dataflow: wkv_b dgrad -> d kv_normed -> clone(x) + rmsnorm_backward (+reduce_rows) -> cat with dk_pe -> mxfp8_quantize -> wkv_a GEMMs.
blockers: Launch-bound small tensors spread over three autograd op(s).

title: Dist-MoE backward staging: backward plan + activation-to-dispatch copy
description: The routed-expert backward recomputes a plan and copies the saved routed input [4096,7168] back into the symmetric dispatch buffer for the forward recompute. Folding the plan into the copy kernel (or keeping the forward dispatch buffer) removes a launch and part of the traffic.
bitwise_notes: Copy + integer planning.
dataflow: saved routed input -> copy_activation_to_dispatch -> recompute fprop GEMMs.
blockers: Dist-MoE internals; the symmetric buffer is shared across layers, so retaining the forward copy needs per-layer buffers.

title: dist_moe routing metadata and plan kernels
description: Inside each routed-expert forward and backward, small kernels split the 8 routes per token by destination rank, build prefix sums and per-expert counts, gather metadata and build the forward/backward GEMM plans.
shapes_dtypes: expert ids int64 [4096,8], weights fp32 [4096,8], per-rank/expert counts and offsets (KB-sized)
bitwise_notes: Prefix sums and slot assignment define the order of routed rows, which downstream data placement depends on.
dataflow: All kernels consume only the [4096,8] routing ids/weights produced by the router (F10); the backward plan recomputes information known from the forward plan.
blockers: Library-internal (dist_moe); plan kernels are split by EP barrier points; backward plan could be cached from forward.

title: attention_norm backward + residual-grad add (layer boundary)
description: Per layer, the wq_a and wkv_a input gradients are added, fed through attention_norm's RMSNorm backward (two kernels), and the result is added to the residual gradient to form the previous layer's output gradient.
shapes_dtypes: bf16 [4096,7168] x4 inputs (two dX, residual grad, saved input), rstd fp32 [4096,1], weight [7168]
bitwise_notes: RMSNorm row reduction and weight-grad column reduction order; separate bf16 rounding of each add.
dataflow: add(dX_wq_a, dX_wkv_a) -> rms_norm_backward -> add(residual grad) -> previous layer's output gradient; each intermediate has one consumer.
blockers: The weight-grad column reduction across 4096 tokens needs a second pass or ordered cross-CTA reduction.

title: MoE router + aux-loss backward and gate-grad hi/mid/lo split
description: Per MoE layer, the backward of the routing weights (normalize, gather), of the load-balance aux loss and of the sigmoid produces the gate-logit gradient [4096,256] fp32, which is then split into hi/mid/lo bf16 parts and concatenated for the 3-way bf16 router-gate GEMMs; about 70 small kernels including a 31-kernel deterministic scatter_add.
bitwise_notes: scatter_add order (deterministic mode) must be reproduced; with only 8 distinct columns per row and no duplicate indices per row, a per-row scatter is collision-free and therefore order-independent.
dataflow: Everything is per-token over a 256-wide row: grad of the 8 selected weights -> scatter into 256 columns -> add aux-loss grad -> sigmoid_backward -> split into three bf16 terms written directly into the [4096,768] GEMM operand.
blockers: Deterministic scatter_add launches a sort-based path (31 kernels); aux-loss pieces come from separate functions; the hi/mid/lo split uses int16 bit tricks saved from forward.

title: kv_norm backward + k_pe grad cat + wkv_a dY quantize
description: Per layer, kv_norm's RMSNorm backward (three kernels on [4096,512]) produces the compressed-kv gradient, which is concatenated with the k_pe gradient [4096,64] into [4096,576] and quantized to MXFP8 for the wkv_a backward GEMMs.
bitwise_notes: RMSNorm reductions; exact amax.
dataflow: rms bwd output and k_pe grad only feed the cat, which only feeds the quantizer; one kernel can write the concatenated fp8 tensor.
blockers: The k_pe gradient comes from fused_mla_kv_backward (B6); the strided [4096,576]->[4096,512] slice forces an extra copy kernel in the norm backward.

title: FSDP pre-all-gather fp32->bf16 parameter cast fused with copy-in (multi-tensor)
description: Before each block's all-gather (forward and backward), every fp32 parameter shard is cast to bf16 by its own kernel (about 10 per block, plus a contiguous clone for dim-1-sharded w13), then _foreach_copy_ copies the bf16 shards into the flat all-gather input. One multi-tensor kernel can read the fp32 shards and write bf16 directly into the all-gather input.
bitwise_notes: Elementwise round-to-nearest cast and copies only.
dataflow: fp32 sharded params -> _to_copy(bf16) -> (clone for movedim'd shards) -> _foreach_copy_ into flat all-gather input -> all_gather; intermediates have no other consumer.
blockers: The cast happens inside torchtitan's FSDP tensor-subclass pre-all-gather <callback> while the copy-in is FSDP's; requires the <callback> to return a dtype-converting view or FSDP to cast during copy-in. Also repeated in the backward re-unshard although parameters did not change.

title: Router + aux-loss backward to the gate-logit gradient
description: The backward of the top-k score masking, aux-loss injection, normalisation, scaling, the gather of scores (deterministic scatter-add implemented with a radix sort), the L1-normalisation of the aux loss and the sigmoid runs ~59 kernels per MoE layer to produce d(gate logits) [4096,256] fp32 from d(topk scores) [4096,8]. Each token row's gradient depends only on that row (plus the scalar aux-loss gradient), so one row-wise kernel suffices.
shapes_dtypes: d topk scores fp32 [4096,8]; scores fp32 [4096,256]; routing map bool [4096,256]; out fp32 [4096,256]
bitwise_notes: Row sums over K=8 and over E=256 (normalize backward) must keep the reduce order; the gather backward is collision-free (top-k ids are unique per row), so the deterministic sort-based scatter-add can become a direct store with identical results.
dataflow: d topk_scores -> MaskedFillBackward -> MulBackward(route_scale) -> DivBackward(norm) -> SumBackward -> GatherBackward (scatter into [4096,256]) + aux-loss path (Mul/Div/Expand/ClampMin/LinalgVectorNorm backward over [4096,256]) -> add_ -> SigmoidBackward -> d gate logits.
blockers: Spread over autograd op(s) of several modules (routed_experts mask, router, aux_loss); requires a custom autograd Function for the router; deterministic scatter_add path for gather_backward.

title: Forward-backward: produce the colwise MXFP8 copy of bf16-saved linear inputs in the forward quantize instead of requantizing in backward
description: wq_a, wkv_a, wq_b, wo, shared/dense w13 and lm_head save their bf16 input and re-read it in backward to quantize colwise for the weight-gradient GEMM; wq_a and wkv_a even quantize the same normed tensor twice. The forward quantization kernel already reads that input and can write the colwise MXFP8 layout too, which is saved instead of being recomputed.
shapes_dtypes: bf16 inputs [4096,7168] (wq_a=wkv_a, w13, lm_head), [4096,1536] (wq_b), [4096,16384] (wo) -> fp8e4m3 colwise + e8m0 scales
bitwise_notes: Same quantizer on the same bf16 tensor gives identical bytes; only the place it runs changes.
dataflow: forward: normed/attention output -> rowwise quantize -> fprop GEMM, bf16 saved; backward: saved bf16 -> colwise quantize (+2 swizzles) -> wgrad GEMM.
blockers: Changes the saved-activation format (memory and recompute policy); the recipe keeps bf16 for shared-input and attention-output projections on purpose; the bf16 normed tensor is not needed by the norm backward, so saving MXFP8 instead reduces memory.

title: Layer-output gradient: routed-expert broadcast-and-scale + shared w2 dY quantize
description: Per layer, the layer-output gradient [4096,7168] is read by two consumers: dist_moe broadcasts it to the 8 routes scaled by the routing weights (also computing the routing-weight gradient against the saved route outputs), and the shared-expert w2 backward quantizes it to MXFP8.
shapes_dtypes: dy bf16 [4096,7168]; saved route outputs bf16 [4096,8,7168]; grad routes bf16 [4096,8,7168]; fp8 [4096,7168] x2 + scales
bitwise_notes: Routing-weight gradient is a dot product over D=7168 (order must match); amax exact.
dataflow: Both consumers read the same dy rows; one kernel can load dy once, quantize it and emit the scaled route gradients.
blockers: One consumer is inside dist_moe.block_scaled_backward (after recompute and barriers), the other is the torchao quantizer.

title: MLA key assembly (K-nope copy + shared rotated k_pe broadcast) in the wkv_b GEMM epilogue
description: fused_mla_kv materialises K [4096,128,192] by copying the nope half of each head from the wkv_b output [4096,128,256] and broadcasting the rotated shared k_pe; V stays a view. The wkv_b GEMM epilogue can write K (with the rope tail) and V directly.
bitwise_notes: Copy + pointwise rotation; needs a GEMM with custom epilogue.
dataflow: wkv_b scaled_mm -> kv -> fused_mla_k_rope (+ k_pe from wkv_a) -> K, V -> flash attention.
blockers: cuBLAS GEMM epilogue; K and V would become separate allocations (V no longer a free view); alternatively an MLA-aware attention kernel reading K-nope and k_pe directly.

title: Attention output MXFP8 quantize + scale swizzle
description: Per layer, the attention output [4096,128,128] bf16 is re-read and quantized to MXFP8 for the wo GEMM, and its scales are swizzled by a separate kernel.
bitwise_notes: Exact amax; swizzle is a fixed permutation.
dataflow: The swizzle reads only the quantizer's scale output; folding it removes one kernel. Further (T3): quantize in the attention forward epilogue.
blockers: torchao quantizer and swizzle are separate ops; attention epilogue belongs to flash-attention.
